# Customer and product configuration endpoints (2026-03-20 05:34Z)

_**User**_

 I added customer and product configuration endpoints in the code agent project. Check the agen-code project here @/Users/gerbert/Documents/workspace_ai/code-agent

I want screens where I can configure the customers and product configurations in the settings menu. 

Here are the original plan details from code-agent backend project:
Phase 1: Customer Registry

1A. Database Migration — V28__create_customer_registry.sql

File: src/main/resources/db/migration/V28__create_customer_registry.sql

Two tables: customers (top-level) and products (child, with environments + teams as JSONB). This follows the same hybrid relational+JSONB pattern used by execution_plans and quality_reports.

CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name          TEXT NOT NULL,
    metadata      JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    display_name  TEXT NOT NULL,
    git           JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    jira          JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    confluence    JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    environments  JSONB DEFAULT '[]',
    teams         JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    metadata      JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_products_customer ON products(customer_id);

Optionally link repo_settings to products:

ALTER TABLE repo_settings ADD COLUMN product_id TEXT REFERENCES products(product_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_repo_settings_product ON repo_settings(product_id);

1B. Domain Records

File: src/main/java/com/eneve/agent/model/CustomerConfig.java

public record CustomerConfig(
    String customerId,
    String name,
    Map<String, Object> metadata,
    Instant createdAt,
    Instant updatedAt
) {}

File: src/main/java/com/eneve/agent/model/ProductConfig.java

public record ProductConfig(
    String productId,
    String customerId,
    String displayName,
    GitConfig git,
    JiraConfig jira,
    ConfluenceConfig confluence,
    List<EnvironmentConfig> environments,
    Map<String, List<TeamMember>> teams,   // role -> members
    Map<String, Object> metadata
) {}

public record GitConfig(String platform, String workspace, String baseUrl) {}
public record JiraConfig(String baseUrl, Map<String, String> projects) {}
public record ConfluenceConfig(String spaceKey, String rootPageId) {}
public record EnvironmentConfig(String name, AwsConfig aws, List<String> deployedRepos) {}
public record AwsConfig(String accountId, String region, String iamRole) {}
public record TeamMember(String name, String email, String jiraAccountId, String slackId) {}

1C. Store — CustomerRegistryStore.java

File: src/main/java/com/eneve/agent/agent/CustomerRegistryStore.java

Follows the exact pattern of RepoSettingsStore.java:





@ApplicationScoped, @Inject AgroalDataSource



Raw JDBC with text-block SQL, PreparedStatement, try-with-resources



Jackson ObjectMapper for JSONB columns



PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE for upserts



Optional<T> for single-row lookups

Key methods:





List<CustomerConfig> listCustomers()



Optional<CustomerConfig> getCustomer(String customerId)



void upsertCustomer(CustomerConfig customer)



boolean deleteCustomer(String customerId)



List<ProductConfig> listProducts(String customerId)



Optional<ProductConfig> getProduct(String productId)



void upsertProduct(ProductConfig product)



boolean deleteProduct(String productId)



Optional<ProductConfig> findByJiraProject(String projectKey) — queries jira JSONB column for a matching project key



Optional<ProductConfig> findByRepoSlug(String workspace, String repoSlug) — joins with repo_settings via product_id

1D. REST Resource — CustomerRegistryResource.java

File: src/main/java/com/eneve/agent/CustomerRegistryResource.java

Follows the exact pattern of SettingsResource.java and MemoryResource.java: @Path, @Produces/@Consumes JSON, OpenAPI annotations, Response return type, Map.of("error", ...) for errors.

Path



Description

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I have a good understanding of the codebase. Let me create a plan for building the customer and product configuration screens.

Here's what I need to do:

1. **Add types** to `src/types/api.ts` for all the customer registry models:
   - `CustomerConfig`
   - `ProductConfig`
   - `GitConfig`
   - `JiraProjectConfig`
   - `ConfluenceProductConfig`
   - `EnvironmentConfig`
   - `AwsConfig`
   - `TeamMember`
   - Request types: `UpsertCustomerRequest`, `UpsertProductRequest`, `UpdateTeamsRequest`, `UpdateEnvironmentsRequest`
   
2. **Create a new page** `src/pages/CustomerRegistry.tsx` with a tabbed interface for managing customers and products, since the data model has customers at the top level with products nested underneath them.

Looking at the product complexity—each one has environments, teams, and various integrations—I'm leaning toward a single `/settings/customers` page where I can select a customer and view their associated products, then drill into individual product details for editing. Though I could also split this into separate menu items for "Customers" and "Products" under Settings, I think a unified registry makes more sense given the dependency relationship. The Customers tab will be a straightforward CRUD list showing customer ID, name, and metadata, while the Products tab displays a filtered list based on the selected customer with a modal for editing complex product details across Git, Jira, Confluence, Environments, and Teams sections. I'll need to add the `/settings/customers` route to the main config and create a menu item under Settings. Looking at existing patterns like `SystemSettings.tsx` and `RepoSettings.tsx`, I'm leaning toward a two-panel layout where the customer list sits alongside the product management interface. customer selected: show products list for that customer
  - Modals for create/edit customer and create/edit product

The product edit modal will need sub-sections (tabs within the modal) for:
1. Basic Info (displayName, customerId, git config)
2. Integrations (Jira, Confluence)  
3. Environments (list of environments with AWS config and deployed repos)
4. Teams (role-based team members)

This is quite complex but follows patterns used in SystemSettings (tabbed sections) and RepoSettings (modal with multiple fields).

Files to create/modify:
1. `src/types/api.ts` - add customer registry types
2. `src/pages/CustomerRegistry.tsx` - new page (create)
3. `src/main.tsx` - add route
4. `src/config/applicationMenu.tsx` - add menu

I'm debating between a tabbed layout versus a master-detail pattern where clicking a customer reveals its products. The master-detail approach feels more natural for the customer → products hierarchy, though the existing codebase leans toward tabs for this kind of nested complexity.

I'll stick with the tab approach since it matches the SystemSettings pattern and keeps the implementation consistent with what's already established. For the menu, I'll add a single "Customers" entry under Settings that routes to the new page, since customers and products are tightly coupled.</details></think>
